findings.summary: The Akai S900 is a 12-bit digital sampler released in 1986 for professional recording studios. It offers a variable sample rate from 7.5 kHz to 40 kHz and 8-voice polyphony. The S900 was succeeded by the S1000 two years later. Version 1.2 firmware added floppy-based OS upgrades, and the final known version was 4.0. An expanded model, the S950, followed in 1988, adding timestretching and a maximum sample rate of 48 kHz. The S900 series uniquely allows samples to loop alternating forwards and backwards. Notable users span hip-hop, electronic, and pop producers.

mechanisms.title: Sample rate conversion
mechanisms.explanation: The S900 uses a variable sample rate ranging from 7.5 kHz to 40 kHz, determined by the 12-bit resolution and internal clock. Lower rates reduce bandwidth and aliasing, shaping the characteristic lo-fi texture associated with the unit.

mechanisms.title: Sample looping direction control
mechanisms.explanation: The S900 series permits a sample to loop alternating forwards and backwards, a feature not available on the S1000 series. This allows rhythmic or tonal reversal effects within a single sample playback.
